spots.summary: The North Carolina State Capitol is the former seat of the legislature of the U.S. state of North Carolina which housed all of the state's government until 1888. The Supreme Court and State Library moved into a separate building in 1888, and the General Assembly moved into the State Legislative Building in 1963.

spots.name: Dix Park
spots.summary: Dix Park is a large urban park in Raleigh, North Carolina, located about a mile southwest of downtown Raleigh. It covers 308 acres (1.25 km2) that were formerly part of the Dorothea Dix Hospital grounds, including a 2.5 acre grass dog park and a 5 acre sunflower field that blooms in July.

spots.name: North Carolina State Fair
spots.summary: The North Carolina State Fair is a U.S. state fair and agricultural exposition held annually in Raleigh, North Carolina. Founded in 1853, the fair is organized by the North Carolina Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services. It attracts around a million visitors over eleven days in mid-October.

spots.summary: Red Hat Tower is the headquarters of the company Red Hat, a subsidiary of IBM. It is located in Raleigh, North Carolina, in the United States. It was completed in 2004 at a cost of $100 million as a headquarters for Progress Energy Inc, a conglomerate of Duke Energy.

spots.name: Dorton Arena
spots.summary: J. S. Dorton Arena is a 7,610-seat multi-purpose arena located in Raleigh, North Carolina, on the grounds of the North Carolina State Fair. It opened in 1952 as State Fair Arena. It has hosted many sporting events, concerts, political rallies, and circuses.

spots.name: Pullen Park Carousel
spots.summary: The Pullen Park Carousel is a classic wood carousel at Pullen Park in Raleigh, North Carolina.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 150 Fayetteville is a 30-story 121.92 m high-rise skyscraper at 150 Fayetteville Street in Raleigh, North Carolina with 544,482 square feet (50,584.0 m2) of space. Completed in 1990, it was one of the downtown Raleigh's two tallest buildings for nearly twenty years, and is currently third tallest.

spots.name: Christ Episcopal Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Christ Episcopal Church, also known as Christ Church on Capitol Square, is an Episcopal church at 120 East Edenton Street in Raleigh, North Carolina. Built in 1848–53 to a design by Richard Upjohn, it is one of the first Gothic Revival churches in the American South.

spots.name: Sacred Heart Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sacred Heart Church is a Catholic church located on Hillsborough Street in downtown Raleigh, North Carolina, United States. The church served as the cathedral of the Diocese of Raleigh from 1924 to 2017.

spots.name: North Carolina Executive Mansion
spots.summary: The North Carolina Executive Mansion is the official residence of the governor of North Carolina and their family. The First Lady of North Carolina is the mansion's official hostess. hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: First Baptist Church of Raleigh is located in downtown Raleigh, North Carolina. The church was the first Baptist church in the city of Raleigh, organized in 1812, and is one of the oldest churches in the area.

spots.name: Briggs Hardware Building

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Briggs Hardware Building is a four-story historic building in downtown Raleigh, Wake County, North Carolina. It was built in 1874 by Thomas Briggs to house his family-owned hardware store. The building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.

spots.name: Carter–Finley Stadium
spots.summary: Wayne Day Family Field at Carter–Finley Stadium is a college football stadium located in Raleigh, North Carolina. It has been home to the NC State Wolfpack football team of the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) since 1966 and has a current seating capacity of 56,919 seats.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Good Shepherd is a historic Episcopal church in downtown Raleigh, North Carolina. The congregation branched off of Christ Episcopal Church in 1874, making it the second oldest Episcopal parish in Raleigh.

spots.summary: First Presbyterian Church is a historic Presbyterian church located at the corner of Morgan and Salisbury Streets in downtown Raleigh, Wake County, North Carolina, United States.

spots.name: Monument to North Carolina Women of the Confederacy
spots.summary: The Monument to North Carolina Women of the Confederacy was installed in Raleigh, North Carolina, United States in 1914. It was designed by Augustus Lukeman. It was located in the surrounds of the North Carolina State Capitol, until its removal on June 21, 2020, during the protests following the murder of George Floyd.

spots.name: Agriculture Building
spots.summary: The Agriculture Building is a historic state government office building located at Raleigh, Wake County, North Carolina. It was built between 1921 and 1923, and is a five-story, Classical Revival. It is sheathed in warm yellow stone, with massive, ashlar veneer, on the ground floor.

spots.name: Capitol Area Historic District
spots.summary: The Capitol Area Historic District is a national historic district located at Raleigh, North Carolina. The district encompasses 25 contributing buildings and was developed after 1792. The district includes notable examples of Classical Revival and Late Gothic Revival style architecture.

spots.name: Royal Baking Company
spots.summary: Royal Baking Company is a historic bakery complex located at Raleigh, North Carolina. The original section was built in 1941, with additions made about 1946–1947, and in the 1960s.

spots.name: Lumsden–Boone Building
spots.summary: The Lumsden–Boone Building is a historic commercial building located at 226 Fayetteville Street in the Fayetteville Street Historic District of Raleigh, North Carolina, United States. Constructed in 1896 for tin and hardware dealer J.C.S.

spots.name: State Bank of North Carolina
spots.summary: The State Bank of North Carolina is the oldest surviving commercial building in Raleigh, North Carolina and was the first state-sponsored banking institution constructed in North Carolina.

spots.name: Duke Energy Center for the Performing Arts
spots.summary: The performing arts center includes 3 primary venues. Memorial Auditorium is the largest and hosts diverse events such as the Carolina Ballet and traveling theater productions of Broadway Series South. Meymandi Concert Hall is home to the North Carolina Symphony. Fletcher Opera Theater is a more intimate setting and hosts events such as Raleigh Chamber Music Guild concerts.

spots.name: Big Boss Brewing company

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Big Boss conducts monthly tours on Saturday afternoons, and it's usually best to check the website to find out exactly when. As with CBC, it's a good idea to get there a bit early, as there's usually a pretty good crowd there. Big Boss brews an assortment of seasonal beers that are distributed locally in addition to their year-round Bad Penny Brown Ale, Helles Belle Belgian Blond, and Angry Angel

spots.name: Krispy Kreme

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The popular Winston-Salem-based doughnut maker is a landmark that nearby residents use to give directions. Look for the "Hot Doughnuts Now" sign for a little round piece of glazed heaven. Quite popular with the students of nearby Broughton and Enloe High Schools, especially in the early morning hours, so plan accordingly.

spots.name: Lilly's Pizza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Part hippie, yuppie, bohemian, and retro, Lilly's is an experience all to its own. It's in the popular Five Points district so parking can be a problem, especially when a popular film is screening at the nearby Rialto theater. If you're adventurous, you can access Five Points by the number 2 CAT bus.

spots.name: Roast Grill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: If you're looking for a hot dog and a bottle of Coke, this is the place in downtown Raleigh. If you're looking for ketchup, though, you may just be asked to leave. Run by a family of Greek immigrants since 1940, in a tiny room added to the front of their house.

spots.name: Big Ed's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Big Ed's signature breakfasts are the Southern standards: homemade biscuits, grits with red-eye gravy, etc. Come Saturday mornings for live Dixieland jazz. Second location on Falls of Neuse Road and Millbrook in Quail Ridge Shopping Center.

spots.name: Raleigh Beer Garden

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Popular spot with a huge selection of beer on tap: North Carolina beers on the first floor and beers from around the world on the second floor. Interesting decor too, with a tree growing in the middle of the first floor.

spots.name: Poole's Downtown Diner

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sourced almost entirely from local farmers and artisan producers, the menu can change on a daily basis. The executive chef, Ashley Christensen, won the 2014 James Beard award for Best Chef in the Southeast.

spots.name: The Raleigh Times Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Snug in the offices of the former Raleigh Times newspaper, this broadsheet turned gastropub is the place for people watching over a pint (or a half pint) of craft-brewed beer.

spots.name: Irregardless Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A Raleigh institution since the 1970s, the Irregardless offers an eclectic menu including creative vegetarian options. Jazz music every night and dancing on Saturday nights.

spots.name: The Fiction Kitchen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Thoughtfully prepared vegan and vegetarian cuisine from a 100% vegetarian kitchen. Very popular among touring music artists playing at the nearby Red Hat Amphitheater.

spots.name: Sushi Nine
spots.summary: A great selection of BOGO sushi rolls offered all day everyday. Also offers a mix of Vietnamese, Thai, Japanese, and Chinese entrees. Full bar.

spots.name: Fox Liquor Bar
spots.summary: A trendy, upscale bar featuring traditional and creative cocktails along with a small, but interesting selection of craft beers.

spots.name: Neomonde

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A delicious Mediterranean market and deli. Their fantastic hummus and baba ghanouj with pita bread alone make any meal great.

spots.name: Farmer's Market Restaurant
spots.summary: Solid, hearty food with fresh ingredients from the state farmer's market right next door. Serves breakfast and lunch.

spots.name: Second Empire Restaurant and Tavern

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Gourmet fare in the restored Dodd-Hinsdale House, built in 1879 in the Second Empire Victorian style.

spots.name: The Pit

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Somewhat upscale whole-hog barbecue. Popular with out-of-staters, but of questionable authenticity.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Brewpub in the warehouse district that opened in 2013.
